advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align module_size_distribution LOC counting with the authoritative gate (use text.count('\n')) so over_cap agrees at the boundary.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:102: `loc = len(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())`
tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py:42: `loc = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape").count("\n")`
The module docstring claims it pins the CURRENT module-size mechanism / the same cap the gate reads, so an LOC-counting mismatch undermines that claim at boundary values.
advisory.finding: module_size_distribution counts LOC with len(text.splitlines()), while the authoritative single-source module-size gate counts LOC with text.count('\n'). For a file without a trailing newline these differ by one, so this metric can report a module as over_cap that the locked gate considers under-cap (and vice versa) at the boundary.
advisory.suggested_fix: Count LOC as read_text().count('\n') to match tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py, or extract a shared LOC helper both call.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle the empty-repo (no commits) case so git-log metrics return zero/empty/None instead of raising CalledProcessError.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:40: `["git", *args],` with `check=True` (line 44)
`git log` on a commit-less repo exits non-zero, so `_numstat_totals` and `cap_change_events` raise instead of returning (0,0)/[]
ABSENCE: no test exercises an initialized-but-empty repo (both test files call _commit before invoking the metrics).
src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:32: `return int((Path(repo_root) / _LIMIT_FILE).read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())`
src/rebar/metrics/registry.py:112: `if result is None:` — the dispatch expects None for 'no data', not an exception
ABSENCE: no test covers a repo_root lacking the limit file.
advisory.finding: The _git helper runs with check=True, so churn / refactor_to_addition_ratio / cap_change_events raise subprocess.CalledProcessError when 'git log' is invoked on a repository with no commits (git exits 128). This unhandled error path is untested and would propagate out of compute() rather than yielding an Unavailable/empty result.
merged_from: _read_cap (and module_size_distribution) raise (FileNotFoundError / ValueError) when the limit file is missing or non-numeric, instead of returning None. evaluate() maps a None compute result to Unavailable; a raising compute breaks that contract and will surface as an exception during registry evaluation for a repo without .github/module-size-limit.txt.
advisory.suggested_fix: Catch CalledProcessError (or pre-check `git rev-parse --verify HEAD`) in _git callers and treat a commit-less repo as empty history.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the git_metrics compute adapter against a missing/None repo_root (return None) instead of letting Path(None)/git-cwd surface.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:245: `repo_root = getattr(ctx, "repo_root", None)` then passed straight to fn
src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:252: `return fn(repo_root)` with no None guard
event_metrics adapter (src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:316-343) similarly reads repo_root but its derivations go through tracker_dir(repo_root).
advisory.finding: The registry context adapter passes a possibly-None repo_root directly into the derivations; when ctx lacks repo_root, Path(None) raises TypeError and _git runs git with cwd=None (the process CWD). The analogous event_metrics adapter routes repo_root through tracker_dir which tolerates such input, so this module is less robust to an underspecified context.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a module_size_distribution test with a module sized within 10% of (but not over) the cap and assert near_cap_count == 1.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:92 `near_threshold = cap * (1 - _NEAR_CAP_FRACTION)`
src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:107-108 `elif loc >= near_threshold:` / `near_cap_count += 1`
test_git_metrics.py:58-60 asserts only count/max_loc/over_cap_count with a cap of 800 and 10/120-line modules (neither near the cap)
test_git_metrics_heldout.py:56-58 asserts only over_cap_count/max_loc with a cap of 50 and 20/90-line modules (one over, one far under — neither in the 45–50 near band)
ABSENCE: no assertion anywhere reads dist['near_cap_count']; a regression zeroing or miscomputing it (wrong fraction, wrong comparator) passes all tests
advisory.finding: near_cap_count and its near-cap threshold branch are never asserted by any test; both module_size_distribution tests use modules far below the near threshold or over the cap, so the `elif loc >= near_threshold` branch is never exercised with an asserted value.
scenarios: A refactor changes _NEAR_CAP_FRACTION handling or the >= comparison and no test fails
A module sized just under the cap is silently not counted as near-cap
advisory.suggested_fix: In a new test, set the cap to 100 and write a module of ~95 lines plus one over-cap module; assert near_cap_count == 1 and over_cap_count == 1.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a refactor_to_addition_ratio test over a range with insertions and zero deletions, asserting the result is 0.0 (not None).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:143-144 docstring: 'A populated range with zero deletions returns ``0.0``; a range with zero insertions returns ``None``'
test_git_metrics.py:72-74 asserts only ratio ≈ 0.4 (insertions and deletions both nonzero)
test_git_metrics_heldout.py:89 asserts only the None (zero-insertions) case
ABSENCE: no test creates a range with insertions but zero deletions to assert the 0.0 result
advisory.finding: The documented refactor_to_addition_ratio contract 'a populated range with zero deletions returns 0.0' is untested; only the 0.4 case and the None-on-zero-insertions case are asserted.
scenarios: A pure-addition commit range where the ratio must be 0.0 (not None/Unavailable)
advisory.suggested_fix: Commit a file addition (insertions>0) with no subsequent deletions in-range and assert refactor_to_addition_ratio(...) == 0.0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs evaluate(spec, ctx) for a registered git spec against a real temp repo context and asserts a MetricValue with the derivation's value, plus that a None context yields Unavailable.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:241-256 `def compute(ctx): if ctx is None: return None; repo_root = getattr(ctx, 'repo_root', None); ...` — the adapter that connects derivations to REGISTRY
test_git_metrics_heldout.py:92-103 test_git_metrics_registered_with_labels asserts only s.id/lens/source and is_authoritative — never calls evaluate() or spec.compute(ctx)
ABSENCE: no test exercises the adapter's None-context guard or attribute extraction; a swapped/renamed attr or missing guard would pass
advisory.finding: The c085 context-adapter compute (_spec) — including its `ctx is None -> None` guard and getattr(repo_root/since/until) extraction — is never invoked; the registration test only inspects spec label fields, so the actual adapter-to-derivation wiring has no behavioral coverage.
scenarios: A context object with repo_root/since/until is passed through evaluate() and must yield the derivation's value
A None context must produce Unavailable (via compute returning None)
advisory.suggested_fix: Build a simple context object (with repo_root/since/until) over a temp repo, look up the 'churn' spec in REGISTRY, call registry.evaluate(spec, ctx), and assert the resulting MetricValue.value matches churn(...); separately assert evaluate(spec, None) returns Unavailable.
